correctness.rationale: Setting R=(I+sL)^-1 yields C=2R-I, with R entries strictly positive on connected graphs for s>0. Augment A by Delta-deg(v) separate stationary ports so its row sums Delta; absolute Neumann series for R has coefficients counting rooted closed port walks. Universal Delta-regular covering-tree reduced-port words inject their closed walks into the original port graph, giving R_vv >= regular-tree g_Delta(s), strictly > for each finite graph because its port system has a non-tree reduced loop (cycle or stationary port). I checked the cavity q=1/[1+sDelta-(Delta-1)s²q] and root g=1/[1+sDelta-Delta s²q], with g(sigma)=1/2 exactly for Delta=3..13 by independent rational arithmetic. g strictly decreases; regular-tree-radius balls converge coefficientwise and via dominated Neumann series to g, so any supercritical s gives a negative center diagonal in a sufficiently large finite ball. I independently enumerated all labelled connected simple graphs on 2..5 vertices, checked rational positivity at the applicable degree cap; finite checks supplement infinite comparison/limit proof. Physical h=2s, strict endpoint positivity of every finite graph holds; Delta>=3.
